fieldDescription: Master switch. Turning this off freezes the war chest economy (existing bases keep operating on vanilla rules).
Your black market trades feed a pirate war chest. Bases earn passive income and pay to launch raids; successful raids return spoils. When the chest covers the next base's cost, the pirates expand.
War chest cost of a tier-2 pirate base. Each tier up or down multiplies by the tier cost growth.
Cost multiplier per tier: at defaults tier 1 ~94k, tier 3 ~240k, tier 4 ~384k, tier 5 ~614k. Higher = strongholds are a bigger investment.

Below this many operating bases the underworld rebuilds its footing: buys the best tier it can afford while reserving enough for another starter base. At or above it, it saves toward a base one tier above its current best.
Shortest pause before rebuilding after a base is destroyed - applied when the war chest is flush.
Longest pause before rebuilding after a base is destroyed - applied when the war chest is empty. Scales down toward the minimum as the chest fills.
Passive war chest income per operating base per month. Tuned so bases sustain their vanilla raid cadence but passive income alone never buys a new base.
Launching a raid costs this many credits per fleet point (tier-1 raid ~100 FP, tier-5 ~450 FP). A base skips its raid if the chest can't cover it.
Fraction of a successful raid's launch cost recouped as spoils.
Additional spoils per size point of hostile markets in the raided system. Repelled raids return nothing.
At game start (or when first enabled), the chest is seeded to fund this many bases, minus any that already exist.
Operating reserve included in the starting war chest seed.
Hard cap on simultaneously operating (raiding) pirate bases. Vanilla is 3.

Destroying a pirate base offsets your lifetime contribution figure by this much (never below zero) - redemption through demolition. Also reduces your income share, helping restore a pierced Piracy Respite.
Destroying ordinary pirate fleets also offsets your contribution, at this many credits per fleet point of the destroyed fleet.

Pirates preying on trade shipping is plunder that flows to the war chest. Every colony sector-wide is checked for shipping disruptions; the pirate-attributable share becomes chest income. Never counts against your own contribution.
Feed the war chest from pirate-caused shipping disruptions sector-wide.
War chest income per point of a disrupted colony's size, times the pirate-attributable fraction, each time its shipping is freshly disrupted.

The underworld collects a monthly cut of the sector's illegal trade - the same commodity flows vanilla routes as smuggling fleets. Income that scales with the economy (including your colonies) instead of your personal habits. Sector income only: it dilutes YOUR share over time.
Feed the war chest a monthly cut of the sector's illegal commodity trade.

Monthly rate applied to each market's illegal trade value at base prices: illegal-source exports plus imports attributed to illegal sources - both ends of a smuggling run pay, so big consumer colonies count too.
Free ports fence everyone's contraband and pay accordingly. Applies to all free ports, yours included - your colonies' cut shows as its own intel line.

With zero operating bases only this fraction of the tithe flows. Eradication buys quiet, but piracy follows civilization - the trickle eventually re-founds a base. 0 = true dormancy (only player trade revives the underworld).

Underworld contacts offer, alongside their job list, commissions for goods no legal market sells - colony-grade industrial equipment and rare blueprints. Deposits go straight into the war chest, and fulfillment is a REAL raid by an operating base against whoever holds the goods. With zero bases the order waits while your deposit finances the rebuild. Deposits count as personal contribution in full, and the raided faction's losses become a receivable in your name.
Underworld-tagged contacts offer the sourcing service alongside their regular jobs - operating bases or not.
Commission price as a multiple of the item's base value.
Equipment is stolen from real colonies: the commission price adds this fraction per 100 points of the source colony's defender + station strength. Sources the network can't crack are greyed out.
Open commissions allowed at once.
Minimum rep with the CONTACT (not the faction) before the sourcing service is offered - same personal-rep gate as vanilla contact missions. One of: NEUTRAL FAVORABLE WELCOMING FRIENDLY COOPERATIVE.

What a contact can source scales with their importance: final commission prices are capped at this figure doubled per importance level (Very Low 150k / Low 300k / Medium 600k / High 1.2M); a Very High contact can get anything.
Ceiling on rotating blueprint offers per market per month; the actual number offered is 1 + the contact's importance level (Very Low 1 ... Very High 5) capped by this.
Fraction of the deposit that becomes debt in your name - the raided faction's losses, bought up by a collection house that knows who paid for the raid.
Deposit fraction refunded when the commissioned raid is repelled.
Deposit fraction refunded when no raid could be mounted at all.
Days the network keeps failing to mount the raid while HAVING an operating base, before refunding. With zero bases the order waits instead (up to a year).
Black market sales are valued at actual demand-adjusted credits, then weighted by usefulness to a pirate war effort. Purchases are plain revenue. Wash-trading (buy-and-sell-back) nets to zero.
Weight on credits you spend buying from the black market.
Weight on weapons and fighter wings sold - these directly arm raiders.
Weight on hulls sold on the black market.
Weight on general commodities (including drugs and organs - the pirates would have fenced those anyway).
Weight on raw ores - of little use to a war effort.
Flat war chest bonus when a blueprint is sold on the black market (the vanilla behavior of pirates learning it still applies).

A defensive fleet stationed on each base so a solo assault faces a real fight, not a bare station. Scales with tier; built with standard pirate generation (uses sold blueprints); re-forms if destroyed while the base stands.
Station a tier-scaled defensive fleet on each pirate base.
Fleet points of a tier-1 base garrison.
Additional garrison fleet points per tier above 1 (tier 5 = base + 4x this).
Days before a destroyed garrison re-forms, if the base still stands.
Vanilla base stations get restored as tier rises, but their defense fleets never grow. With scaling on, higher-tier bases field more and bigger patrols.
Tier 3: +1 medium patrol. Tier 4: +1 medium +1 heavy. Tier 5: +2 medium +2 heavy.
Patrol fleet size multiplier at tier 5 (scales linearly from 1.0 at tier 1).

Vanilla posts 40k-80k by tier, sized for defenses that never grow. With scaling on, the bounty on a war-chest base grows with the fight it puts up: tier-1 figure plus a step per tier (40/105/170/235/300k at defaults).
Scale base bounties with tier. Off = vanilla's pirateBaseBounty1..5.
Bounty on a tier-1 base, before the +/-10% jitter and rounding to 10k.
Additional bounty per tier above 1 (tier 5 = tier-1 figure + 4x this).

Piracy Respite is vanilla's permanent reward for defeating the pirate crisis. But wariness fades when the war chest overflows with YOUR money: past these thresholds, chest-funded bases resume preying on your colonies (activity penalties and ambient fleets - never raids). Stop contributing and your share dilutes until the respite returns.
Allow chest-funded bases to ignore Piracy Respite when the thresholds below are met.
Your lifetime black market contribution must exceed this for wariness to fade.
Your share of the underworld's lifetime income must exceed this for wariness to fade.

OPTIONAL, OFF BY DEFAULT - switch it on below. You do not get a price on your head - you get a BILL. Value fenced through a faction's black market becomes a receivable in your name, bought up at a discount by an independent collection house that compounds it monthly and sends ONE collector fleet, at full strength. There is no pay-off button: a debt is settled fleet-to-fleet when the collector catches you. Lose that fight and they take payment out of your holds. Destroy every ship with an officer aboard and the debt dies with the crew; let one get away, or run, and the same crew finds you again. Stop paying on terms and the house sells your paper to the pirates, who quote figures they invented.

Master switch for debt accrual, collection notices, collector fleets and the whole pay-or-fight encounter. Off by default. Safe to flip either way mid-campaign: off, every collector stands down and goes home the moment you save this panel, nothing accrues, nothing is billed, and any balance already on the books sleeps; back on, that balance wakes with its notice and grace periods restarted from that day.

What the faction lost is the tariff it would have collected had the same cargo crossed its docks legally - not the cargo's full value, which was never theirs. Debt accrues at this fraction of the value you fed the pirates. 0.3 matches vanilla's standard 30%% tariff. The war chest still receives the full amount.
No debt accrues while the market's smuggling suspicion is below this (the suspicion level from the black market tooltip - transponder-off trading generates none).
The evaded tariff is attributed to you in full at this suspicion level, scaling linearly below it. 0.3 = "high" suspicion.
Monthly compounding while the independent collection house holds the paper. 0.03 is about 43%% a year - expensive, but survivable.
Monthly compounding once the pirates hold it. 0.06 is about 101%% a year - the balance doubles annually, and they do not send letters.
No collector is dispatched below this balance - it is not worth the fuel. Protects the first hour of a new game.
Days after the debt opens that the written collection notice arrives. You always learn the debt exists before it can hurt you.
Days after the debt opens before any collector can spawn. Clamped in code to at least the notice period, so lowering this can never get you ambushed before the letter arrives.
Chance per roughly 10-day check, once past the grace period, that a collector is dispatched. Doubled while the creditors are enforcing after missed payments.

THE collector's fleet points as a fraction of YOUR combat fleet points. There is only ever one, sent at full strength from the first day - no ladder of smaller fleets, no escalation, no second crew while the first is alive. Sizing off your fleet rather than off the balance in credits is what makes a doomstack structurally impossible; 1.2 is what the old escalation curve only reached at its cap.

Floor on the collector's fleet points - itself clamped in code to your own combat FP, so the floor can never hand a two-frigate player something bigger than they are. Raising it above your fleet does nothing.
Hard ceiling on the one collector's fleet points. A safety net - the FP Ratio above is what sizes it.
How long a collector hunts you before giving up and turning for home. A crew that gives up, or dies to somebody who is not you, is replaced on the next spawn roll.
Flat burn levels a collector may add so it can actually catch you. 0 = no help, and a fast fleet outruns the whole system.

fieldName: House Sells Paper When Its Crew Dies
fieldDescription: THE OFFICER RULE's one fork. Off: destroy every ship with an officer aboard and the debt dies with the crew, whoever holds the paper. On: destroying the HOUSE's crew makes the house cut its losses and sell your paper to the pirates instead, and it is their crew whose officers have to die - a two-act arc, with the pirate act reachable by fighting rather than only by defaulting on terms.

Once the pirates hold your paper they ALWAYS inflate the figure - never an honest quote. The multiplier is rolled once per collector and frozen, and the quote is rounded to something suspiciously round.
Upper end of the invented multiplier, before the surcharge for comm links you have cut.
Added to the pirate markup for every comm link you have cut on a collector. Running is allowed and the same crew simply keeps hunting - the only price is on the next lie.

Story points to call a pirate crew on an invented figure. Your true balance is always printed beside their quote, so this is never a gamble. The audit is permanent for that debt: every later quote is honest. 0 hides the option entirely.

On terms you pay the holder's interest PLUS this fraction of the principal each month, so the balance falls by exactly this much monthly whoever holds it and the plan always terminates - roughly 11 months.
Floor on a monthly installment, so a small plan finishes instead of dripping forever.
Miss a payment and this fraction of the SHORTFALL - not of the balance - is added back to what you owe.
Consecutive missed installments before the creditors start enforcing: spawn interval halved, spawn chance doubled.

Consecutive missed installments before the house gives up and sells your paper to the pirates, regardless of your combat record - the second road into the pirate act for a player who never fires a shot.
How long an enforcement window lasts after it opens.

fieldName: Pirate Rep per House Crew Finished
fieldDescription: Reputation points GAINED with the pirates for destroying the last officer of a collector crew working for the independent house - the underworld appreciates its patron handling the opposition. Capped so it can never take you past friendly. 0 = off.

fieldName: Pirate Rep per Pirate Crew Finished
fieldDescription: Reputation points LOST with the pirates for destroying the last officer of a collector crew working the underworld's OWN paper - once they hold your debt, the collectors you shoot are theirs. Bounded so it can never fall past suspicious. 0 = off.

A debt collector collects BY FORCE. Lose a stand-up fight to one and boarding parties take credits first, then cargo by value, until the balance is covered - and the balance drops by what they took. They never take people, AI cores, or your last supplies and fuel. Off = losing costs you nothing but the ships.
Seized cargo is credited against the balance at this fraction of base value - a hold full of goods is worth less to a collector than the same figure in cash. 1.0 = full value.
Units of supplies a seizure will never touch, so being caught in deep space is a setback and not a soft-lock.
Units of fuel a seizure will never touch, so being caught in deep space is a setback and not a soft-lock.
Whether special items - blueprints, nanoforges and the like - can be taken in a forced collection. AI cores are always exempt.
Show exact war chest figures in the intel screen. Off = vaguer flavor descriptions.
Verbose starsector.log output.
